---
title: "Generator"
subtitle: "The families -C/-D/-E/-W, the scale options, and the instances they build"
---

Without `-d`, `zeno` builds the instance with a family of generating functions, from the options `-n -t -p -C -D -E -W -r -j -k -l -m -x -y`
([command line](../solver/cli.qmd#instance-options)). Every option means what its name says:
`-C` sets the **costs**, `-D` the **durations**, `-E` the **$C_I$-side** and `-W` the
**$C_G$-side** durations. The construction is `legacy::buildInstance`
(`src/zeno/legacy_input.cpp`).

## Generating functions

`-C`, `-D`, `-E` and `-W` each take a code:

| Code | Function $f(k)$ | Name in the suites |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | $\ln k$ | `log` |
| 2 | $\sqrt k$ | `sqrt` |
| 3 (default) | $k$ | `linear`, identity |
| 4 | $2^k$ | `pow2` |
| 5 | $5\lfloor k/2 \rfloor + 0.1\,(k \bmod 2)$ | `staircase`, the "(5/2)$i$" family |

Any other code falls back to the identity. The argument $k$ is truncated to an unsigned integer
before $f$ is applied.

## Construction

For cities $i = 1, \dots, n$, with $r$ = `-r`, $(j, k)$ = `-j -k`, $(l, m)$ = `-l -m` and $(x, y)$ =
`-x -y` (defaults $r = 1$, $j = l = x = 1$, $k = m = y = 0$):

1. Costs on increasing arguments, durations on **decreasing** ones:
   $$c_i = x\,f_C(\lfloor j\,i + k \rfloor) + y, \qquad d_i = x\,f_D(\lfloor l\,(n+1-i) + m \rfloor) + y.$$
   With `-E` and `-W` (both needed; `-D` is then ignored) the instance is non-symmetric:
   $$d_i = x\,f_E(\lfloor l\,(n+1-i) + m \rfloor) + y, \qquad \bar d_i = x\,f_W(\lfloor l\,(n+1-i) + m \rfloor) + y.$$
   Otherwise $\bar d = d$.
2. Every value is multiplied by $r$ and truncated toward zero: $v \leftarrow \operatorname{trunc}(r\,v)$.
   `-r 100` keeps slowly growing functions such as $\ln$ from collapsing onto a few integers.

With increasing functions, the first city is the slowest and the cheapest: faster cities cost
more, which is what makes the front non-trivial. The order of the cities does not matter to the
front.

## Examples

These are the outputs of `zeno generate` (durations, then costs; 3 lines when non-symmetric):

| Options | Instance |
|---|---|
| `-n 4` (defaults, linear) | $d = (4, 3, 2, 1)$, $c = (1, 2, 3, 4)$ |
| `-n 4 -C 2 -D 2 -r 10` | $d = (20, 17, 14, 10)$, $c = (10, 14, 17, 20)$ |
| `-n 10 -D 1 -r 100` | $d = (230, 219, 207, 194, 179, 160, 138, 109, 69, 0)$, $c = (100, 200, \dots, 1000)$ |
| `-n 10 -D 1` | $d = (2, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0)$, $c = (1, 2, \dots, 10)$ |
| `-n 4 -E 3 -W 2 -r 10` | $d = (40, 30, 20, 10)$, $\bar d = (20, 17, 14, 10)$, $c = (10, 20, 30, 40)$ |

Zero values are allowed and do occur: $\ln 1 = 0$, so the log family has a city of duration or
cost 0.

## The families in the suites

The `families` suite runs every family on $n = 10$, $t = 8$, $p = 3$
([suites](suites.qmd#suite-families)): `linear` (`-C 3 -D 3`), `log` (`-C 1 -D 1 -r 100`), `sqrt`
(`-C 2 -D 2 -r 100`), `pow2` (`-C 4 -D 4`), `staircase` (`-C 5 -D 5 -r 10`), and the mixed
`log-linear` (logarithmic durations and linear costs, `-C 3 -D 1 -r 100`) and `sqrt-linear`
(`-C 3 -D 2 -r 100`). The default family is the only one with a closed-form front
([known fronts](known-fronts.qmd)). The others need the general algorithm, and on them a greedy
schedule of the landings can miss points.

Every instance the generator builds without `-E`/`-W` is symmetric, and every PDDL problem `zeno`
writes from it satisfies (A1), so its front is exact.
